- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior peak), model often overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% above recent high.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤ 0.33) within 3–5 days, model fails to adjust downward; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% per negative sentiment day.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon; if forecast is >10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 1–3%.
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.33–0.67), model often overfits recent volatility; use 10-day moving average as baseline for correction.
- Forecast errors are more pronounced in early 30-day window (days 1–7); apply 1–2% downward correction for first 7 days if sentiment is weak or neutral.
